tagline: Search any US-listed ticker, open the stock, and get its price chart, a plain-English business summary, recent news and an AI read on whether it fits your style of investing.
summary: Trade Stocks Using AI starts with a search box backed by Nasdaq's full list of US exchange-listed securities. Open a stock to see its latest quote and a daily price chart (Yahoo), a two-to-three sentence summary of what the company does (found by reading its official homepage), and shared recent headlines refreshed on demand.

Signed-in users can keep a **My stocks** list and ask for **investment thoughts**: Claude weighs the summary, headlines and chart indicators and says whether the stock looks suited to buy-and-hold, a one-year view or day trading. An operator console lists users and KPIs and resyncs the Nasdaq symbol catalog. Auth and data live in Supabase.
audience: Retail investors who want a quick, readable first look at a ticker.
People comparing a handful of stocks they're watching.
notFor: Trading or brokerage — no orders, no portfolio balances.
Financial advice — AI thoughts are an opinion grounded in public material.
Real-time or intraday data — latest quote and daily bars only.

capabilities.title: Ticker search
capabilities.detail: Landing search matches ticker or company name against the stored Nasdaq Trader catalog (`/api/stocks/search`).

capabilities.title: Stock detail
capabilities.detail: `/stock-detail-page`: company name, latest price (`POST /api/stocks/:id/quote`) and daily chart with range picker (`GET /:id/chart`).

capabilities.title: Business summary
capabilities.detail: Finds the official homepage, reads it and stores a short summary on the listing (`POST /:id/business-summary`).

capabilities.title: News
capabilities.detail: Shared recent headlines per stock, refreshed on demand (research only if nothing new in 24h).

capabilities.title: Investment thoughts
capabilities.detail: Claude's read on buy-and-hold vs one-year vs day trading, grounded in summary, news and chart (`POST /:id/investment-thoughts`).

capabilities.title: My stocks
capabilities.detail: `/stocks` and `/dashboard`: a signed-in user's watch list (`/api/user-stocks`).

capabilities.title: Auth
capabilities.detail: Supabase email/Google sign-in, password reset, `/auth/callback`; Express syncs a `public.users` row from the JWT.

capabilities.title: Operator console
capabilities.detail: Users list and KPIs, Nasdaq catalog sync, analytics stub (no JWT; operator only).

components.name: Web app
components.stack: Next.js, Redux Toolkit, Supabase JS, Vercel Analytics
components.owns: Landing search, stock detail, dashboard, My stocks, auth. Calls the API at `NEXT_PUBLIC_EXPRESS_URL` with the Supabase JWT.

components.name: API
components.stack: Express + TypeScript, Supabase JS, Anthropic SDK
components.owns: Symbol catalog, Yahoo quotes and charts, homepage research and news (Apify + Claude), investment thoughts, user stocks, account sync, operator APIs. Schema in `supabase/migrations/`.
components.doesNotOwn: Login — Supabase does that in the browser.

components.name: Operator console
components.owns: Users list and KPIs, Nasdaq catalog sync, analytics stub.

dataFlow: The operator syncs the Nasdaq Trader symbol file into `stocks` from the console.
Users sign in with Supabase in the browser; the web sends the JWT to Express, which upserts `public.users`.
Opening a stock refreshes its quote and chart from Yahoo.
Business summary and news use Apify to find/read pages and Claude to summarize; results are stored on the listing and shared by everyone.
Investment thoughts send the summary, headlines and indicators to Claude and store one row per request.

trust.title: Browser
trust.detail: Supabase anon key and its JWT.

trust.title: API
trust.detail: Supabase service role, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `APIFY_API_TOKEN`. Operator routes take no JWT — keep the console private.

trust.title: Third parties
trust.detail: Yahoo for prices, Apify for web research, Anthropic for summaries and thoughts.

commonTasks.title: Run locally
steps: Run **Setup** in Hub (add the console path to hub.local.json if you need it).
Set `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `APIFY_API_TOKEN` on the API (there's no `.env.example`).
Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_EXPRESS_URL` and the Supabase public vars on the web, then **Run**.
Sync the Nasdaq catalog from the console so search returns results.

commonTasks.title: Research a stock
commonTasks.when: You want a quick read on a ticker.
steps: Search on the landing page and open the stock.
Refresh news and the business summary if they're stale.
Sign in and request investment thoughts; add it to My stocks to watch it.

troubleshooting.fix: The symbol catalog is empty — run the Nasdaq catalog sync from the console.
Yahoo didn't recognize the symbol mapping or rate-limited; try again or check `to-yahoo-symbol`.
The web and API point at different Supabase projects, or no session reached Express.

glossary.definition: `stocks` rows loaded from Nasdaq Trader's listed-securities file.
AI assessment of fit for buy-and-hold, one-year or day trading.

hubNotes: `trade-stocks-using-ai-console` is in the registry and cloned at `~/github/tradestocksusingai/`, but hub.local.json has no path for it.
Neither web nor API has a `.env.example`; the variables above come from the code.
No local Postgres — data lives in Supabase. READMEs are still templates; the ADRs (web 015–023, express 010–019) are the real docs.
